description: We are a team of ambitious minds driven by curiosity, creativity, and a passion for innovation. At NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in Madinah, we aim to push boundaries and explore fresh ways to connect science, technology, and imagination. Our mission is to turn complex Earth data into meaningful, interactive experiences that inspire curiosity and make science more accessible to everyone.
summary:
Earth's Symphony is an interactive web platform that transforms real NASA nighttime light data into meaningful sounds, allowing people to explore changes on Earth through hearing rather than sight alone.

Earth observation data is traditionally presented through images, maps, and visual comparisons, creating accessibility barriers for blind and visually impaired individuals and people unfamiliar with interpreting scientific maps.

To address this challenge,  Earth's Symphony uses NASA's Black Marble nighttime light data to convert light intensity into musical tones. Brighter areas produce higher-pitched sounds, enabling users to hear differences in illumination across cities and explore changes between 2012 and 2023.

By connecting sound with scientific data, Earth's Symphony provides an engaging way to recognize patterns, compare nighttime light changes, and explore possible urban development over time.

Our goal is to make Earth science more accessible, inclusive, and emotionally engaging, transforming complex visual information into an experience that anyone can listen to, explore, and understand.
details:
Earth's Symphony is an interactive web platform that transforms NASA nighttime light data into meaningful sounds, making Earth observation more accessible.

How It Works: Python is used for spatial data processing, extracting and normalizing image-derived light intensity values across 12 years (2012–2023). The processed data is organized into spatial grids, allowing users to explore nighttime illumination and hear differences through musical tones.

Technologies and Tools:

  • Python: Spatial data processing, normalization, and preparation.
  • HTML, CSS, JavaScript: Interactive web development.
  • Three.js & WebGL: 3D Earth visualization.
  • Web Audio API: Real-time data sonification.
  • Canvas API: Image brightness processing.
  • Web Speech API: Spoken accessibility feedback.
  • JSON: Processed data metadata.
  • NASA Nighttime Lights: Source imagery.

Benefits and Impact: Earth's Symphony helps users, including blind and visually impaired individuals, explore changes in nighttime illumination through sound, encouraging scientific curiosity and inclusive learning.

Innovation: Earth's Symphony combines spatial data analysis, interactive Earth visualization, and sound to create a multisensory scientific experience.

Key Considerations: Scientific accuracy, consistent data normalization, accessibility, usability, and meaningful sound representation.
